messages.subject: sub setting for geom_smooth
parts:
I have a plot & a linear model.  I'd like to plot the prediction with confidence interval on the plot. 
Here is how I've made the predictions

#model
fake.lm <-lm(zGrade ~ 1+ Rep + ISE + P7APrior+HSGPA +MATH+Years+Female+White+Course+Course*P7APrior, data= Master.complete[Master.complete$Course != "P7A",])

#grid to predict over
nd.years <- expand.grid(#SID = 999999999, # nuisance variable don't care about it
                        Rep = as.logical(levels(factor(Master.complete$Rep))),
                        ISE = levels(factor(Master.complete$ISE)),
                        P7APrior = levels(factor(Master.complete$P7APrior)),
                        Female = levels(factor(Master.complete$Female)),
                        White = as.logical(levels(factor(Master.complete$White))),
                        HSGPA= mean(Master.complete$HSGPA),
                        MATH = mean(Master.complete$MATH),
                        Course =levels(factor(Master.complete$Course))[2:14], # not including P7A level,
                        Years =seq(min(Master.complete$Years),
                                    max(Master.complete$Years),
                                  by= 0.125))
#predictions and errors
nd.years$zGrade <- stats::predict(fake.lm, newdata=nd.years)
err <- stats::predict(fake.lm, newdata=nd.years, se = TRUE)
nd.years$ucl <- err$fit + 1.96 * err$se.fit
nd.years$lcl <- err$fit - 1.96 * err$se.fit


#plotting
p.Years <- ggplot(Master.complete, aes(x = Years, y = zGrade))
p.Years <- p.Years + geom_point(aes(color = ISE, shape = Female, 
                                    fill = colorfill, 
                                    alpha =1/10))
show(p.Years)
p.Years <- p.Years +  scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "blue")) 
#p.Years
p.Years <- p.Years +  scale_shape_manual(values = c(23, 21))  
p.Years
p.Years <- p.Years +  scale_fill_manual(breaks = c("Not White", "White"), # use breaks to tell it which labels to plot
                                        values = c("blue", NA, "red", NA))   # use NA to tell it to only fill the NotWhite ones
p.Years <- p.Years +  theme_bw() 

p.Years <- p.Years + geom_smooth(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), 
                                  data=nd.years[nd.years$Rep==FALSE&
                                                       nd.years$ISE=="nonISE"&
                                                       nd.years$Female=="Female"&
                                                          nd.years$White ==TRUE&
                                                          nd.years$Course=="B2C",],
                                  stat="identity")
p.Years <- p.Years +  xlab("Years at UC Davis") +ylab("Normalized Grade")
p.Years




As one can see the fitted data has  discontinuities.  I commented out another approach I tried to just plot the prediction for some values of the other variables.  I am expecting 3 lines, one each for P7APrior =-1,0,1. 

Any help would be greatly appreciated
Robert

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: sub setting for geom_smooth
parts:
You haven't given us a reproducible example--e.g. a simple data set and code that runs it--which makes things harder. But:

-- You'd only get three geom_smooth lines if, in its (or the plot) aes() call, there was a 'linetype= P7APrior' or 'color= P7APrior' setting. Try adding this.

-- But...I don't understand why you're setting ymin and ymax in the aes() call, as geom_smooth() doesn't understand these aesthetics (see its help page).

-- What I suspect you want to do is ditch geom_smooth entirely, since you've already fit linear models in the code above, and use geom_line(aes(y= P7APrior)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=lcl,ymax=ucl)). Or something like that.

Hopefully this makes sense and is useful. Again, for more specific help, please post a fully reproducible example.

Ben
